To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a procedure of the bench simulation of the long-term interaction of polymer films with flows of atomic ogygen and VUV radiation in the ionosphere is developed; (2) the efficiency of the bench simulation is proved by the results of satellite experiments; (3) the dependences of degradation rates of polymer films on atomic oxygen fluxes are determined; (4) the synergetic effect in the ablation of polymer films is found.
the bench experiments of the long term action of atomic oxygen on polymer materials in a flow of atomic oxygen are in good agreement with the satellite measurements.
the physical simulation of the longterm interaction of polymer materials in the ionosphere is possible and the procedure of such a simulation was designed and tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical simulation of the longterm interaction of polymer materials in the ionosphere of the earth and in other space environments.
the development of methods for bench simulation of the action on polymers of the space ionosphere environment.
the bench simulation of the action on polymer materials of atomic oxygen and ultraviolet radiation in a low earth orbit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bench experiments are an effective and reliable method to study the interaction of polymer materials in the space environment.
the physical simulation of polymer degradation is an effective tool for the prediction of polymer materials behavior under conditions of long term exposure in the ionosphere and space.
the bench measurements of polymer degradation in the earth's atmosphere are an adequate method for forecasting the long term degradation of polymers in the near satellite space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bench simulation of the action on polymer materials in a space ionospheric environment is possible, and it allows one to forecast the long term behavior of materials in space.

the bench simulation of the action on polymer materials in space is an effective tool of investigation of the influence of the near satellite space environment on the materials and allows one to forecast the service life of materials in the ionosphere and to select the best materials for space application.

the bench measurements of the degradation of the polymers in the near space environment can be used to determine the time changes of their mass and geometric parameters during the whole operating time in the space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now predict with a high degree of accuracy how long a polymer film will survive in the space environment.
it is possible to simulate the action of the atomic oxygen and vacuum-ultraviolet radiation on polymers in the earth's upper atmosphere using bench measurements.
the bench experiments can be used to predict the long-term degradation of polymer films in the ionosphere.
